data.title: Chile's jobless rate rises to 10% in quarter through October
data.description:
Chile's unemployment rate hit 10% in the quarter through October, statistics agency INE said on Friday, above the 9.8% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

The Andean country's jobless rate also rose from 9.8% in the previous rolling quarter.

data.title: Nasdaq futures surge as investors pile back into battered AI stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 1.29%, S&P 1.64%, Nasdaq 2.23%
  • Chipmakers, AI hyperscalers and neoclouds jump
  • Gold and silver miners rally, tracking metals price recovery

By Shashwat Chauhan and Niket Nishant

US stock futures surged on Friday, led by a more than 2% jump in Nasdaq 100 contracts, as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday lull and rushed back into battered AI-linked shares.

Wall Street's main indexes have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI trade.

Investors have alternated between bargain-hunting after a steep selloff and concerns over soaring costs, heavy borrowing and whether the investments are generating sufficient returns.

"There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets," Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Despite the turbulence, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are headed for their best week since April and August, respectively, while the blue-chip Dow is on track for its strongest week since April 2025.

However, the gains have done little to erase November's losses. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are on course for their worst November since 2008, pressured by concerns over tougher AI regulation following the Democrats' midterm election victory and expectations that monetary policy will remain restrictive.

Investors are also assessing the impact of the Trump administration's proposed new tariffs, announced on Wednesday, on imports from 14 trading partners.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated further in October.

All three major indexes entered a technical correction this month, with the Nasdaq 100 at one point falling nearly 20% from its October peak.

At 6:42 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 646 points, or 1.29%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 118 points, or 1.64%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 581.25 points, or 2.23%.

Nvidia, at the center of the AI boom, gained 3.6% in premarket trading, though the stock remained more than 37% below its October record high based on its last close.

Other chipmakers battered this month also rebounded, with AMD climbing 4.4% and Broadcom gaining 3.4%.

AI hyperscalers Alphabet , Amazon.com , Microsoft , Meta Platforms and Oracle rose between 2.1% and 4.4%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius advanced 6.5% and 7%, respectively. Other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm Sandisk, optical-products maker Lumentum and server maker Dell, also gained.

Gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered from a bruising few sessions. Newmont gained 5%, while the Global X Silver Miners ETF advanced 5.7%.

Altria slid 2% after the Marlboro maker said it was considering a possible all-cash bid for Imperial Brands and was discussing a deal involving part of the British tobacco group's business with another party.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell 7.5% after the US Food and Drug Administration extended its review of the company's kidney-disease drug by up to three months.

Trading volumes could be light following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday, with US equity markets open for only a half day on Friday.

data.title: Search Minerals Announces C$1.4 Million Secured Convertible Loan
data.description:
St. Lewis, Newfoundland and Labrador--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Search Minerals Inc. (OTC Pink: SHCMF) ("Search Minerals" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding term sheet (the "Term Sheet") with certain lenders (the "Lenders"), including two of the Company's largest shareholders, Petra Holdings Company Inc. ("Petra") and Harder Investments Ltd. ("Harder"), for the Lenders to provide the Company a C$1.4 million secured convertible loan (the "Loan"). The proceeds from the Loan will be primarily used to repay the Company's C$700,000 principal amount convertible note issued to Texas Critical Minerals, LLC ("TCM") in October 2024, which matured on October 25, 2025, together with all accrued interest.

The principal amount of the Loan will mature and be repayable in full on the date which is three years from closing, and will be convertible into common shares at the option of the Lenders at any time prior to the close of business on the maturity date at a conversion price of $0.30 per share. The principal amount of the Loan will bear interest at 8.5% per annum, payable annually on December 31, commencing December 31, 2027. Subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV"), Search will have the option to pay interest in common shares in lieu of cash at the market price for the common shares at the time the interest becomes payable. Any conversion that would result in a Lender becoming a Control Person (as defined in the policies of the TSXV) will be subject to prior TSXV approval, including shareholder approval. The Loan will be secured by a pledge of the shares of the Company's subsidiaries Alterra Resources Inc. and 86857 Newfoundland & Labrador Inc., together with guarantees and personal property security granted by those subsidiaries.

Upon completion, the transaction is expected to:

  • Lower interest rate costs: reduce the interest rate on the TCM note being repaid from 15% to 8.5%;
  • Reduce TCM's claims: resolve the claim TCM has filed against the Company relating to the note, one of three claims filed by TCM against the Company as disclosed in the Company's financial statements. With respect to the two remaining claims, the Company continues to dispute the amounts alleged to be owing, believes it has credible defences, and intends to defend its position while remaining focused on advancing its core projects and protecting shareholder interests; and
  • Improve working capital: remove past-due debt owed to TCM from the Company's working capital deficit, subject to final accounting treatment, by extending the maturity dates for the Company's debt and treating such liability as non-current, and provide funds for general working capital.

Jonathan Beigle, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Search Minerals, commented: "We appreciate the continued support of our largest shareholders. This financing allows us to repay the TCM note, lower our interest costs and extend maturities. This will allow us to focus all of our effort on advancing our projects for the benefit of all shareholders."

Closing of the transaction is expected in mid-December, 2026. The Term Sheet is a preliminary binding agreement; completion of the transaction remains subject to, among other things, negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, approval of the Company's Board of Directors and a special committee of independent directors, acceptance of the TSXV, and satisfaction of customary conditions. There can be no assurance that the transaction will be completed on the terms described or at all.

The Loan, and any common shares issued on conversion of the Loan, will be subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance of the Loan, in accordance with applicable securities legislation and TSXV policies. Any common shares issued in payment of interest will be subject to a hold period of four months and one day from their date of issuance.

Petra is controlled by Michael Pearson, a director of the Company, and Petra also owns more than 10% of the voting securities of the Company. Accordingly, Petra is a "related party" of the Company. Harder owns more than 10% of the voting securities of the Company. Accordingly, Harder is also a "related party" of the Company. As a result, the transaction is a related party transaction subject to Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The transaction is exempt from the formal valuation requirements of MI 61-101 pursuant to subsection 5.5(b) of MI 61-101 because the Company's common Shares are listed only on the TSXV and is exempt from the minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 pursuant to subsection 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 because neither the fair market value of the subject matter of, nor the fair market value of the consideration for, the transaction, insofar as it involves interested parties, exceeds 25% of the Company's market capitalization as determined in accordance with MI 61-101.

ABOUT SEARCH MINERALS

Led by a proven management team and board of directors, Search is focused on finding and developing Critical Rare Earth Elements (CREE), Zirconium (Zr) and Hafnium (Hf) resources within the emerging Port Hope Simpson - St. Lewis CREE District of southeast Labrador. The Company controls a belt 64 km long and 2 km wide that is road accessible, on tidewater, and located near three local communities. The Company has completed a preliminary economic assessment report with resource estimates for Foxtrot and Deep Fox. It is also working on four exploration prospects along the belt: Fox Meadow, Silver Fox, Fox Run and Awesome Fox.

The Company has completed two pilot plant operations and produced highly purified mixed rare earth carbonate concentrate and mixed REO concentrate for separation and refining.

All material information on the Company may be found on its website at www.searchminerals.ca and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

data.title: Economic Data Likely to Keep Pressure on Bonds Next Week — Market Talk
data.description: The macroeconomic data flow is expected to remain on the bond-bearish side next week, LBBW's Elmar Voelker says in a note. Eurozone inflation might have stabilized at around 4% in November, with falling energy prices providing some relief, the senior fixed-income analyst says. "Initial data from France and Spain even suggest that hopes for an easing of inflation pressures may be justified," he says, However, the core rate is likely to have risen for the third month in a row, he adds. In the U.S., attention will be primarily focused on November labor-market data, Voelker says. LBBW expects solid growth of around 100,000 jobs and a stable unemployment rate. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Crypto Stocks Gain After Bitcoin Tops $61K In Tech Rebound, But Analysts Want A Move Above $62K
data.description:
Key points:
  • Analyst Ted Pillows said Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 for a rally toward $65,000.
  • MN Fund founder Michael van de Poppe said Bitcoin has held the $57K region, with targets of $68,000 to $72,000.
  • Gold, silver and oil prices were also on the rise. 

Large-cap crypto-linked stocks rose in early-morning trade on Friday as Bitcoin (BTC) climbed above $61,000, alongside a rebound in tech futures. Analysts said Bitcoin still needs to reclaim $62,000 to extend the rally.

Bitcoin treasury Strategy (MSTR) rose over 6% in pre-market trade, while Bitcoin’s price rose 1.6% in the last 24 hours to around $61,600. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, and sentiment around Bitcoin rose to ‘extremely bullish’ from the ‘bullish’ zone.

Tech Rebound Lifts Stocks, Silver And Gold

The gains came as the tech rebound extended after ticking higher on Wednesday. Tech-heavy Nasdaq futures were up 2.45% at the time of writing, while S&P 500 futures gained around 1.8%.

Retail sentiment around the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) trended in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) moved to ‘extremely bullish' from the ‘bullish’ zone.

Anthropic (ANT), which made its public market debut last week, was up around 3.6% in pre-market trade, with sentiment simmering to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day. Nvidia (NVDA) was up around 3.5%, with sentiment trending in the ‘bullish’ zone.

Memory stocks Micron (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) rose more than 9% each, while CipherDigital (CIFR) and CoreWeave (CRWV) gained around 8% each.

Commodity and oil prices were also on the rise. Silver’s price jumped 7% to above $44 an ounce, while gold gained 2.5% to above $3,670 an ounce. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 2% to reclaim $85 a barrel.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) moved to ‘neutral’ from the ‘bearish’ zone over the past day, while sentiment around SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) remained in ‘bearish’ territory. Sentiment around the United States Oil Fund (USO) trended in the ‘bullish’ zone.

Analysts Want Bitcoin To Reclaim $62,000

Crypto analyst Ted Pillows said buyers are still in the market. "$BTC spot buyers are still there," he wrote on X. "Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 now for a rally toward $65,000.”

MN Fund founder Michael van de Poppe said Bitcoin looks good in the short term. "It's held the $57K region and made a higher low, after which a short uptrend was established," he wrote on X. "Targets remain $68,000-72,000.”

Crypto Stocks Gain After Bitcoin Tops $61K

Bitcoin treasury Strive (ASST) and Tom Lee-backed Ethereum (ETH) treasury Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) also gained in pre-market trade. ASST stock rose over 7%, while BMNR stock gained around 5%.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ASST trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around BMNR trended in the ‘bullish’ zone.

Bitcoin miners pivoting into the AI trade were also trading higher. MARA Holdings (MARA), TeraWulf (WULF), CleanSpark (CLSK), and CoreScientific (CORZ) each rose over 6% in pre-market trade.

USDC stablecoin issuer Circle (CRCL) and cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase (COIN) gained around 4% each.

HYPE Leads Gains Among Crypto Large-Caps

Hyperliquid (HYPE) led gains among the top 10 cryptocurrencies by market capitalization. HYPE’s price jumped nearly 10% in the last 24 hours, reclaiming the $65 mark. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Hyperliquid dropped to ‘bearish’ from the ‘neutral’ zone over the past day.

Solana (SOL) gained around 3.5%, Ripple’s XRP (XRP) climbed 2.7%, while leading altcoin Ethereum (ETH) rose 1.6%. Sentiment around Solana and Ethereum trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around XRP remained in ‘bearish’ territory.

The uptick weighed on short sellers, with 71.4% of the $240 million liquidated in the last 24 hours coming from short positions. Bitcoin shorts accounted for $83.18 million and Ethereum shorts for $55.77 million.

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Key Labor Data in Focus Ahead of Fed's December Rate Decision
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff

Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting Nov. 30.

U.S. labor market data, including the key nonfarm payrolls report, will be in focus ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Dec. 9.

The data will provide the market with clues on how much scope the Fed has to raise interest rates further, including whether another hike is possible in December.

In Europe, provisional November inflation data will be released for individual eurozone countries and the wider single currency area, which will influence rate expectations for the European Central Bank.

In Asia, monetary policy will be in focus, with speeches by the Japanese and Australian central bank chiefs likely to offer clues on the prospects for further interest-rate hikes, while India's central bank will hold its policy meeting. A slew of purchasing managers' indexes, including those from China, will shed light on the region's economic momentum heading into year-end, while trade and inflation data from South Korea and parts of Southeast Asia will also draw attention.

U.S.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls data for November are due on Dec. 4, a key data point ahead of the Federal Reserve's decision whether or not to raise interest rates again in December after a pause in October.

Markets are pricing in a December hike as economic data have continued to be relatively solid overall, while inflation has remained above the central bank's target.

Alongside the Labor Department's monthly update, ADP will release its private payrolls data on Wednesday and the JOLTS job openings data for October are due Tuesday along with weekly jobless claims on Thursday.

ISM will release two reports for November, manufacturing data on Tuesday and services data on Thursday. Final S&P manufacturing and services purchasing managers' surveys for November will be released on Tuesday and Thursday, respectively.

The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment reading for December will be published on Dec.4, a key indicator as the holiday retail sales season gets into full gear.

Other data include the Chicago ISM business barometer and the Texas manufacturing survey on Monday, construction spending on Tuesday and factory orders on Thursday.

Canada

Employment data for November and third-quarter economic growth figures are the main events in Canada in the coming week.

The gross domestic product data will be released on Monday while the jobs data are due on Dec. 4.

The latest GDP data showed the economy grew at an annual rate of 3.3% in the second quarter. Canada's jobs market remained weak in October, however, losing 4,700 jobs following back-to-back job declines in August and September. The unemployment rate rose 0.2 percentage points to 6.7% in October.

U.K.

The Bank of England will release the money and credit report on Monday, which indicates the amount of borrowing and deposits by U.K. households and businesses.

The Nationwide House Price Index for November will be released on Tuesday. Analysts expect that higher mortgage rates might have lowered demand in the housing market, causing prices to fall. "We suspect that house prices may have dipped in November, which would leave the annual pace of house price growth at just 0.2% year on year," Investec economists said in a note.

The Bank of England will publish the monthly decision maker panel data for November on Dec. 4. The data is based on a survey of chief financial officers (CFOs) from small, medium, and large U.K. businesses and provides insights on businesses' inflation and wage growth expectations.

The final U.K. purchasing manager index survey data for November are due next week. The manufacturing PMI data will be published on Tuesday, the services PMI data on Thursday and the construction PMI data on Dec. 4.

Eurozone

Inflation data take center stage next week, starting with German consumer price data for November on Monday, followed by flash estimates for eurozone inflation on Tuesday. Eurozone annual inflation climbed to 4.0% in October from 3.8% in September, though data for France and Spain on Friday showed inflation falling more sharply than expected in November as fuel prices declined.

Final eurozone manufacturing purchasing managers' index data for November will also be released on Tuesday. The flash reading climbed to a two-month high of 52.9 from 52.7 in October.

That will come before unemployment data for the eurozone on Wednesday, final services PMI data on Thursday and retail sales figures for October on Friday.

Switzerland

Switzerland's consumer prices data for November on Wednesday will be closely monitored for any further signs of increased price pressures after annual inflation rose sharply to a higher-than-expected 1.5% in October from 1.0% in September. Headline inflation is likely to climb a bit further, Capital Economics economist Harry Chambers said in a note.

"However, core inflation should remain very low and the headline rate should remain within the Swiss National Bank's 0-2% target range."

The SNB will therefore probably leave interest rates unchanged, he said.

Poland

Poland's central bank announces its policy decision on Wednesday. Monetary Policy Council member Ireneusz Dabrowski recently stated that Poland's October economic data support keeping interest rates unchanged at the December meeting, suggesting that rates are sufficiently restrictive.

"This aligns with our call that the National Bank of Poland will not hike rates until the first quarter of next year," ING analyst Frantisek Taborsky said in a note.

Japan

On Monday, all eyes will be on Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda's remarks in the central Japanese city of Nagoya as investors look for hints on whether the bank will raise its policy rate to 1.50% in December from the current 1.25%, as widely expected.

Ueda has recently reiterated the bank's readiness to hike interest rates further and voiced caution over the risk of underlying inflation overshooting its 2% target.

Other economic indicators due during the week include October industrial production and retail sales data on Monday, followed by the jobs report and November auto sales figures on Tuesday.

The Ministry of Finance is scheduled to auction two-year government bonds on Monday and 10-year notes on Thursday.

Australia/New Zealand

The week ahead in Australia will be dominated by a speech made by Michele Bullock, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, on Tuesday.

Bullock's comments will come as financial markets are digesting recent news of yet another increase in the inflation rate, which has prompted talk that interest rates might need to rise further. Still, labor market data is showing that unemployment is also going up as firms trim staff numbers in response to a slowdown in the economy.

Some economists estimate that the rise in inflation represents a peak, and that the RBA will have some scope to cut interest rates by the middle of next year. Others expect the RBA to remain cautious and keep rates at their current 18-year highs in order to ensure inflation returns to target.

Bullock has been hawkish in recent comments and the last inflation report will grant little room to back away from her stance.

The RBA is also monitoring a big drop in house prices, and signs lending for new homes is collapsing.

It is a delicate time for the RBA, which has already made clear that it faces difficult choices.

China

It's all about PMIs in China, with a string of gauges of manufacturing, services and construction activity set to show the strength of economic momentum midway through the final quarter of the year.

Things kick off Monday with official surveys, followed by private-sector manufacturing and services PMIs on Tuesday and Thursday, respectively.

Goldman Sachs expects the official manufacturing PMI to edge up to 49.5 in November from 49.3 in October, supported by an uptick in steel production, though the reading would still signal a contraction in factory activity.

The private-sector RatingDog manufacturing PMI, compiled by S&P Global, is expected to reflect stronger port activity in coastal regions, GS said.

GS expects the official nonmanufacturing PMI to fall to 49.4 from 49.7, as construction activity likely remained subdued and services activity faced seasonal weakness.

Asia PMIs

A slew of monthly manufacturing PMI readings for Asia are due on Tuesday, including Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and in Southeast Asia. The surveys will be closely watched as cost pressures and higher rates could continue to weigh on business confidence and operating conditions.

Flash PMI data showed that private-sector business activity remained divergent, with inflation and manufacturing production trends differing across economies against the backdrop of geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties.

India

It's a big week for India, with the expected release of its latest quarterly economic growth data, which could inform the central bank's monetary policy decision later in the week.

ANZ expects India's GDP data for the July-September period, due Monday, to come in stronger than market expectations, which would prompt the Reserve Bank of India to hike interest rates on Dec. 4. "Strong GDP growth would likely give the RBI room to focus more on inflation," Dhiraj Nim of ANZ said in a note.

A sudden rise in equity inflows has helped stabilize the rupee, which substantially reduces the odds of an outsized 50-basis-point hike, but inflation risks have risen, Nim said.

UOB economist Jester Koh expects the RBI to deliver a unanimous 25-basis-point rate hike, as India's inflation has breached the upper end of RBI's tolerance band, with signs of broadening price pressures across non-food components and persistently higher food inflation. Recent liquidity absorption measures rolled out by authorities should help strengthen monetary-policy transmission, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of rate hikes, Koh said.

About Bradda Head Lithium Ltd.

Bradda Head Lithium Ltd is a North America-focused lithium development group. The Company's principal interests include the Basin Project, comprising Basin East and Basin West, and the San Domingo Project in Arizona.

The Basin East Project has a Measured Mineral Resource of 20 Mt at an average grade of 929 ppm Li, containing 99 kt LCE; an Indicated Mineral Resource of 122 Mt at an average grade of 860 ppm Li; and an Inferred Mineral Resource of 499 Mt at an average grade of 810 ppm Li. Together, these categories contain 2.81 Mt LCE. A plan of operations for the Basin West area was approved by the Bureau of Land Management in 2025, and the Company is progressing the associated Environmental Assessment.

The San Domingo Project comprises 248 claims covering approximately 1,850 acres, located primarily on Bureau of Land Management land, together with two Arizona State Land Department claims. To date, 108 drill holes totalling 13,089 m have been completed across three drilling campaigns. More than 1,000 pegmatites have been mapped across the project area; 18 have been identified as priority targets and six have been drill-tested. Two Notices of Intent are active, and updated drilling plans may be implemented once the required permits have been secured. The next exploration phase is intended to further delineate prospective areas and assess their potential to support a Mineral Resource Estimate prepared in accordance with NI 43-101.

The Whistlejacket Project comprises nine Arizona State Land Department Mineral Exploration Permits covering 2,010.7 hectares. The project is subject to a definitive option-to-joint-venture agreement with Kennecott Exploration Company and targets spodumene-bearing pegmatites.

Kennecott's previous exploration included 19 diamond drill holes totalling 4,188 m, all of which intersected lithium mineralisation. Reported results include 51.0 m at 1.11% Li₂O in hole WSTL0009 and 19.47 m at 1.66% Li₂O in hole WSTL0008. Surface mapping, sampling, airborne geophysics and high-resolution aerial imagery have also contributed to the geological dataset for the project.

The Group intends to continue advancing its three principal projects in Arizona while seeking to realise value from its other prospective pegmatite and brine assets in Arizona, Nevada and Pennsylvania.

data.title: Zydus Lifesciences Falls 3% After US FDA Delays Approval Of Key Drug; Brokerages Differ On Outlook
data.description:
Bernstein maintains an ‘Outperform’ rating on Zydus Lifesciences, with a target price of Rs 1,457, implying an upside of around 22 per cent from the previous close

Shares of Zydus Lifesciences declined on Friday, November 27, after the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) issued a complete response letter (CRL) for the company’s new drug application (NDA) for saroglitazar. The development has prompted differing views among brokerages, with some expecting a manageable delay in the drug’s launch, while others see an opportunity in the stock’s recent weakness.

The CRL follows the USFDA’s October 2026 inspection of Zydus Lifesciences’ Moraiya manufacturing facility, which resulted in five Form 483 observations. The inspection has not yet received a final classification from the regulator. The USFDA typically communicates its classification within 90 days of completing an inspection.

JPMorgan said the CRL appears to be linked to the resolution of the inspection observations rather than deficiencies relating to the drug or its clinical data. The brokerage has retained a ‘Neutral’ rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,250, implying an upside of 4.6 per cent from the previous closing price.

According to JPMorgan, although the regulatory setback has pushed approval beyond the November 2026 Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target date, timely remediation could still allow the company to proceed with its planned commercial launch in March-April 2027.

The brokerage also pointed to an approval for an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) from the Moraiya facility after the inspection as a positive indicator of its regulatory standing. It expects limited near-term earnings impact, given its estimated saroglitazar revenue contribution of USD 9 million in FY28 and USD 63 million in FY29. The facility accounts for around 13 per cent of Zydus Lifesciences’ overall revenue, with no major approvals pending from the site, it added.

However, JPMorgan flagged a prolonged remediation process or an adverse facility classification as key risks.

Bernstein Sees Buying Opportunity

Bernstein has maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating on Zydus Lifesciences, with a target price of Rs 1,457, implying an upside of around 22 per cent from the previous close.

The brokerage believes investors could be overestimating the implications of the CRL by applying the timelines typically associated with generic drug approvals. It views the current weakness in the stock as a potential buying opportunity.

Bernstein noted that saroglitazar is a new chemical entity (NCE) under priority review and is awaiting regulatory clearance, while the manufacturing facility continues to address the Form 483 observations. It has retained its expectation of a March-April 2027 commercial launch.

The brokerage also sees a reasonable possibility of the Moraiya facility receiving a ‘No Action Indicated’ (NAI) or ‘Voluntary Action Indicated’ (VAI) classification within the USFDA’s usual 90-day inspection window. It expects greater clarity on the regulatory pathway and launch timeline in December.

Zydus Lifesciences shares fell as much as 3.2 per cent to an intraday low of Rs 1,156.50 on Friday. The stock was trading 2.8 per cent lower at Rs 1,160.40, trimming its year-to-date gains to 28 per cent.

data.title: IDFC First Bank Gains 3%, Nears 52-Week High on Growth Prospects
data.description:
Shares of the private sector lender climbed 3 per cent in intraday trade, moving closer to their 52-week high of Rs 89.58

Shares of IDFC First Bank rose 3 per cent in intraday trade on Friday, approaching their 52-week high as expectations of sustained loan and deposit growth supported investor sentiment. The stock gained even as the broader market traded lower.

The private sector lender's shares climbed to Rs 88.95 on the BSE, close to the 52-week high of Rs 89.58 recorded on 23 September 2026. Brokerage firm Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 100, citing the bank's medium-term growth prospects, improving funding mix and potential expansion in return on assets (ROA).

Stock Performance And Market Activity

IDFC First Bank shares advanced 3 per cent to Rs 88.95 on the BSE during Friday's intraday session. The stock was trading near its 52-week high of Rs 89.58, reached 23 September 2026.

In comparison, the benchmark BSE Sensex was down 0.2 per cent at 84,158.93 around 9:40 am. A combined 7.3 million shares of IDFC First Bank changed hands on the NSE and BSE, indicating heightened trading activity in the counter.

Deposit Growth And Lower Funding Costs

The bank's management reiterated its expectation of sustaining loan growth of more than 20 per cent in the medium term, supported by expansion of its network and increased corporate lending.

Deposit growth is expected to remain marginally higher than loan growth, which could help reduce the bank's loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR). The lender is also strengthening its current account franchise through lending relationships, technology platforms and services. These initiatives are expected to lower funding costs and improve returns from corporate lending, according to Jefferies. Growth in rural, retail and small and medium enterprise (SME) segments is also expected to support lending yields and margins.

data.title: Garware Hi-Tech Films Appoints Anand H Sharma As CFO
data.description:
The finance professional brings over 24 years of experience across corporate finance, fundraising, compliance and mergers and acquisitions

Garware Hi-Tech Films has appointed Anand H Sharma as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP), effective 26 November 2026. Sharma brings over 24 years of experience in finance and accounts, corporate compliance, business strategy and financial management, having held senior leadership positions across listed companies.

Sharma joins Garware Hi-Tech Films from Carysil, where he served as Executive Director, Chief Operating Officer (COO) and Group CFO. His experience spans financial strategy, debt and equity fundraising, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), cross-border transactions, investor relations, taxation, treasury and regulatory compliance.

A commerce graduate, Sharma is a qualified Chartered Accountant, Company Secretary and Cost and Management Accountant. He completed his Chartered Accountancy qualification in 1998, Company Secretary qualification in 2013 and Cost and Management Accountancy qualification in 2021.

Extensive Finance Leadership

Sharma served as Executive Director, COO and Group CFO at Carysil from November 2015, according to his professional profile. During his tenure, his responsibilities covered finance leadership, accounting and cross-border transactions.

Before joining Carysil, he worked at Batliboi as Vice President of Finance, Accounts and Company Secretary from January 2008 to October 2015. His responsibilities included group financial consolidation, consortium banking, statutory and internal audits, transfer pricing and compliance with stock exchange and Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) requirements.

Experience Across Industries

Sharma previously served as Group CFO at Lactose (India) from November 2005 to January 2008. His responsibilities included raising funds from banks, managing a preferential issue and handling taxation, company law matters and regulatory compliance.

Earlier, he worked as General Manager of Finance and Accounts at Konark Synthetics from December 2000 to October 2005. He also began his professional career as a partner at Bhuwania and Agrawal Associates, where he worked from January 1999 to November 2000.

Focus On Corporate Finance

Sharma's professional experience includes debt and equity fundraising, structured finance, working capital management, cash flow planning, financial modelling and group consolidation. He has also worked on international business management, enterprise resource planning implementation, insurance matters and board meeting management.

His background in financial strategy and corporate compliance brings experience across several core finance functions to his new role at Garware Hi-Tech Films.

Strengthening Finance Leadership

The appointment adds a finance professional with experience in corporate funding, regulatory compliance and business strategy to Garware Hi-Tech Films' leadership team. Sharma's responsibilities as CFO will place him at the centre of the company's financial management and reporting functions.

data.title: Tata Steel-APL Apollo Deal Tests Minority Shareholder Rights
data.description:
SEBI is examining the transaction structure amid concerns over valuation, debt funding and whether interconnected deals should attract related-party safeguards

The proposed Rs 28,000-crore acquisition of Tata Steel's tubes and colour-coated steel businesses by APL Apollo Tubes has triggered questions over corporate governance, after the steelmaker separately agreed to acquire control of the smaller company. The transaction, announced on November 22 and 23, 2026, has drawn objections from proxy advisory firms and institutional investors over its financial implications for minority shareholders.

The scrutiny centres on whether the different components of the arrangement should be assessed as a single transaction under related-party rules, given that Tata Steel is acquiring the promoter's stake in APL Apollo while the latter is purchasing businesses from Tata Steel. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is examining the structure, amid concerns over the acquisition valuation, debt burden, and the extent to which public shareholders have a say in the arrangement.

How The Tata Steel-APL Apollo Deal Is Structured

Under the agreement, APL Apollo will acquire Tata Steel's tubes business for Rs 11,700 crore and its colour-coated steel business, Tata Steel Colors, for Rs 16,300 crore. The combined consideration is Rs 28,000 crore, which APL Apollo plans to initially fund through borrowings.

Separately, Tata Steel has agreed to acquire approximately 26.6 per cent of APL Apollo from its promoter group for around Rs 15,510 crore, at Rs 2,100 per share. It has also announced an open offer to acquire up to an additional 26 per cent from public shareholders at Rs 2,301.40 per share. If the proposed stake purchase and the open offer are completed in full, Tata Steel's holding could rise to more than 50 per cent, giving it control of APL Apollo.

The arrangement also includes a contract-manufacturing agreement involving promoter-linked SG Tech Engineering/SG Spectra for colour-coated steel capacity. This is among the interconnected elements that proxy advisory firms want regulators to examine.

Why Minority Shareholders Are Raising Concerns

The central concern is the distribution of financial risks and benefits between the promoter and public shareholders. While APL Apollo will take on substantial borrowings to finance the business acquisition, its existing promoter group will receive a significant sum through the sale of its stake to Tata Steel.

Investors who continue to hold APL Apollo shares could therefore remain exposed to the company's enlarged debt burden and the risks associated with integrating the acquired businesses. The terms of any subsequent equity fundraise, and the proposed restructuring of the company's capital structure are also important to determining the eventual impact on shareholders.

Related-Party Rules At The Centre Of The Debate

The timing of the board approvals has become a key part of the governance debate. APL Apollo approved the acquisition of Tata Steel's businesses before Tata Steel formally acquired a stake in the company. Consequently, the asset purchase was not classified as a related-party transaction at the time of approval.

However, proxy advisory firms argue that the asset acquisition, promoter stake sale, open offer and contract-manufacturing arrangement should be assessed together rather than as separate transactions.

Under SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements framework, material related-party transactions require shareholder approval, with related parties barred from voting on the resolution. The regulatory framework was strengthened through changes that took effect in April 2023, extending safeguards to certain transactions with unrelated entities where the purpose and effect are to benefit related parties.

The question is whether the interconnected arrangements in the Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal fall within the scope of these provisions. If regulators determine that the relevant transactions attract related-party safeguards, the approval process and the voting rights of minority shareholders could become central to the deal's progression.

The Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction is now drawing attention to the effectiveness of these safeguards. SEBI's examination of the deal, along with the response of institutional investors and proxy advisory firms, could have implications for how complex corporate transactions involving listed companies are structured and approved.

data.title: Puneet Das Steps Down As Britannia Industries CMO
data.description:
Das, who took charge in February 2026, will exit the company on 9 December , citing plans to pursue opportunities outside the organisation

Puneet Das has stepped down as Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries, citing plans to pursue opportunities outside the organisation. His last working day will be 9 December 2026, according to an intimation filed with the stock exchanges.

In his resignation letter, Das stated, "After due consideration, I have decided to move on from my role at Britannia to pursue opportunities outside the organisation. Please treat this letter as my formal resignation from the position of Chief Marketing Officer. I would like to request that I be relieved on 9th December 2026 and would appreciate your consideration of the same."

Das took over as Britannia Industries' CMO on 11 February 2026. His departure comes less than a year after assuming the role.

He brings over 24 years of experience across the FMCG sector in India and international markets, having held senior leadership positions at several consumer goods companies.

Prior to joining Britannia, Das spent over a decade at Colgate-Palmolive. His earlier stints include leadership roles at Marico, PepsiCo India, GSK Consumer Healthcare India and Tata Consumer Products.

During his career, he has worked across brands including 7Up, Boost, Horlicks, Tata Tea and Tetley, building experience across brand management, marketing strategy and consumer businesses.
